scene: Inside a firelit Viking hall at night, Brand, huge and expressive in the foreground (slim young man, cream round face, long light-brown hair tied at the neck, no beard, pale blue tunic, grey-green cloak, one thin silver ring on his arm, black mitten hands), sits hunched over a smoking oil lamp, sweating and counting syllables on his fingers with a panicked stare, while behind him on a high seat a stern bearded jarl in a fur-trimmed red cloak waits with folded arms, pale dawn light already showing at the doorway, and a sharp-nosed rival poet in a black cloak smirking by the fire. Visible hardship: one night, eight perfect lines, or else.

In driving rain on a muddy forest track in Sweden, Brand, huge and expressive in the foreground (long light-brown hair plastered by rain, pale blue tunic, soaked grey-green cloak), stands at the bolted wooden door of a turf-roofed farmhouse with his hand raised to knock and a look of exhausted disbelief, while an old woman peers through a crack in the door shaking her head, smoke and the glow of a ceremony leak from the roof hole, and his two companions sit on a log nursing their sore feet. Visible hardship: a court poet, a hundred miles of forest, and no door that will open.
